claims.text: Cause: lateral stretch of the neck during delivery, from shoulder dystocia, breech extraction, or hyperabduction of the neck.
claims.quote: Brachial plexus injuries frequently follow lateral stretching of the neck during delivery caused by shoulder dystocia , breech extraction , or hyperabduction of the neck in cephalic presentations.

claims.text: Upper plexus (C5 to C7): shoulder and elbow muscles.
claims.quote: Upper brachial plexus (C5 to C7): Affects muscles around the shoulder and elbow

claims.text: Entire plexus: the whole arm, often with T1 sympathetic fibers.
claims.quote: Entire brachial plexus: Affects entire upper extremity and often sympathetic fibers of T1

claims.text: Erb palsy (C5 to C7): shoulder adducted and internally rotated, forearm pronated.
claims.quote: It is an upper brachial plexus (C5 to C7) injury causing adduction and internal rotation of the shoulder with pronation of the forearm.
claims.locator: Brachial Plexus Injuries in Neonates, Erb palsy

claims.text: Same-side diaphragm paralysis from phrenic nerve injury is common.
claims.quote: Ipsilateral paralysis of the diaphragm due to phrenic nerve injury also is common.
